```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Sarathy JP, Blanc L, Alvarez-Cabrera N, et al. Fluoroquinolone
  efficacy against tuberculosis is driven by penetration into lesions and
  activity against resident bacterial populations. *Antimicrob Agents
  Chemother.* 2019;63(5):e02516-18.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02516-18> (open access,
  [PMC6496041](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6496041/))
* Plasma PK parameters reprinted from: Pienaar E, Sarathy J, Prideaux B, et al.
  *PLoS Comput Biol.* 2017;13(8):e1005650,
  <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005650>

The paper compares three fluoroquinolones in rabbits with active tuberculosis.
Its "multi-compartment PK model" (Materials and Methods, *Computational
modeling methods* (iv); Supplemental Figure S3A) couples a two-compartment oral
plasma model to three site-of-action compartments: uninvolved ("normal") lung,
the cellular areas of caseous granulomas, and the caseum of caseous granulomas.
The paper fits it separately for each drug, so the package has one model per
drug:

```{r models}
models <- c(
  moxifloxacin = "Sarathy_2019_moxifloxacin_rabbit",
  gatifloxacin = "Sarathy_2019_gatifloxacin_rabbit",
  levofloxacin = "Sarathy_2019_levofloxacin_rabbit"
)
mods <- lapply(models, readModelDb)
```

The paper also uses GranSim, an agent-based spatial granuloma model (Pienaar
2017), to predict cellular-granuloma concentrations (Figure 1, Table 2 and the
"Cellular granuloma" row of Table S3). GranSim is a hybrid agent-based and
partial-differential-equation simulator and is not reproduced here; the
`lesion` compartment of these models is the multi-compartment model's
"cellular areas of granulomas" state, calibrated to laser-capture
microdissection data, which is a different quantity.

# Population

Female New Zealand White rabbits (2.2 to 2.6 kg) were infected by nose-only
aerosol with *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* HN878 and developed mature cellular
and necrotic lung lesions (Materials and Methods). The plasma PK parameters
come from a nonlinear mixed-effects fit (SimBiology, stochastic EM, constant
error model) to infected rabbits dosed daily by oral gavage: moxifloxacin 25 or
60 mg/kg (n = 4 + 8), gatifloxacin 40 mg/kg (n = 3), levofloxacin 65 or
100 mg/kg (n = 3 + 4) (Pienaar 2017 Table 6). The site-of-action rate constants
were calibrated by nonlinear least squares to drug concentrations in lung
tissue, cellular lesion areas and caseum after a single oral dose of
moxifloxacin 100 mg/kg, gatifloxacin 100 mg/kg or levofloxacin 75 mg/kg.

```{r population}
str(mods$moxifloxacin()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every value comes from Supplemental Table S1 of Sarathy 2019. The plasma rows of
that table are identical to Table 3 of Pienaar 2017, whose footnote states that
the values are "mean and % coefficient of variation determined by non-linear
mixed effects modeling".

| Parameter | MXF | GTX | LVX | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lka` (1/h) | 0.9 (CV 57%) | 0.46 (77%) | 1.25 (50%) | Table S1, ka |
| `lq` (L/h/kg) | 2.86 (12%) | 1.15 (44%) | 0.5 (174%) | Table S1, Q |
| `lvc` (L/kg) | 5.35 (9%) | 1.27 (39%) | 3.48 (10%) | Table S1, Vp |
| `lvp` (L/kg) | 80.8 (0.9%) | 90 (1.5%) | 130 (2%) | Table S1, Vpe |
| `lcl` (L/h/kg) | 1.3 (27%) | 1 (61%) | 0.82 (96%) | Table S1, CL |
| `lk_central_lung` (1/h) | 4.4 | 1.8 | 3.6 | Table S1, k pl-lung |
| `lk_lung_central` (1/h) | 0.6 | 0.5 | 3.3 | Table S1, k lung-pl |
| `lk_central_lesion` (1/h) | 6.5 | 1.8 | 1.5 | Table S1, k pl-cell |
| `lk_lesion_central` (1/h) | 0.7 | 0.5 | 0.7 | Table S1, k cell-pl |
| `lk_central_caseum` (1/h) | 1.8 | 2.1 | 1.2 | Table S1, k pl-cas |
| `lk_caseum_central` (1/h) | 0.3 | 0.8 | 0.6 | Table S1, k cas-pl |
| `etal*` variances | `log(1 + CV^2)` | | | Table S1 %CV; lognormal sampling (Pienaar 2017, *Plasma PK model*) |
| `addSd` | `fixed(0)` | | | Constant error model, magnitude not reported (Pienaar 2017, *Plasma PK calibration*) |
| Plasma ODEs | | | | Pienaar 2017, *Plasma PK model* |
| Site-of-action ODEs | | | | Figure S3A; Materials and Methods (iv); see Assumptions |

# Replicate Supplemental Figure S3B (single dose, typical values)

Figure S3B shows the calibrated model after the single doses used in the lesion
PK studies. The maintainers read the peak concentrations off the figure by eye;
they are approximate (about 1 mg/L).

```{r fig-s3b}
single_dose <- c(moxifloxacin = 100, gatifloxacin = 100, levofloxacin = 75)

solve_typical <- function(drug, events) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mods[[drug]]()), events = events) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = drug)
}

single_events <- function(dose) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  )
}

sim_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(single_dose), function(d) {
  solve_typical(d, single_events(single_dose[[d]]))
}))

sim_sd_long <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::select(drug, time, Plasma = Cc, Lung = Clung, Cellular = Clesion, Caseum = Ccaseum) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(drug, time), names_to = "site", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(sim_sd_long, aes(time, conc, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Supplemental Figure S3B of Sarathy 2019 (MXF and GTX 100 mg/kg, LVX 75 mg/kg)."
  )
```

```{r fig-s3b-check}
fig_s3b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,          ~site,      ~peak_fig,
  "moxifloxacin", "Plasma",   7.5,
  "moxifloxacin", "Lung",     34,
  "moxifloxacin", "Cellular", 47,
  "moxifloxacin", "Caseum",   20.5,
  "gatifloxacin", "Plasma",   13,
  "gatifloxacin", "Lung",     29,
  "gatifloxacin", "Cellular", 29,
  "gatifloxacin", "Caseum",   25,
  "levofloxacin", "Plasma",   12.5,
  "levofloxacin", "Lung",     13,
  "levofloxacin", "Cellular", 21,
  "levofloxacin", "Caseum",   17
)

peaks <- sim_sd_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, site) |>
  dplyr::summarise(peak_model = max(conc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig_s3b, by = c("drug", "site")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (peak_model - peak_fig) / peak_fig)

peaks |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(peak_model, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Site" = site, "Model peak (mg/L)" = peak_model,
    "Figure S3B peak (mg/L, read by eye)" = peak_fig, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value peak concentrations against Figure S3B.")

# A deterministic typical-value solve. Every peak is within 7% of the
# eye-read figure (realised -3.1% to +6.1%); a mis-transcribed rate constant or volume moves the
# affected peak by far more than 15%.
stopifnot(nrow(peaks) == 12L, all(abs(peaks$pct_diff) < 15))
```

The near-identical gatifloxacin lung and cellular curves follow from Table S1,
which gives the same pair of rate constants (1.8 and 0.5 1/h) for both sites.

# Steady state at the human-equivalent doses (Table S3)

The paper simulates 14 days of once-daily dosing at the human-equivalent doses
(moxifloxacin 60 mg/kg, and 25 mg/kg for the low-exposure arm; gatifloxacin
40 mg/kg; levofloxacin 100 mg/kg) and reports AUC0-24 in plasma and caseum.
Because each site compartment is driven by plasma concentration without
returning mass to it, its steady-state AUC is exactly
`k_central_site / k_site_central` times the plasma AUC. This is the
structural fact the check below tests.

```{r arms}
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,           ~drug,          ~dose,
  "MXF 60 mg/kg",       "moxifloxacin", 60,
  "MXF 25 mg/kg",       "moxifloxacin", 25,
  "GTX 40 mg/kg",       "gatifloxacin", 40,
  "LVX 100 mg/kg",      "levofloxacin", 100
)

ss_grid <- seq(13 * 24, 14 * 24, by = 0.25)

ss_events <- function(dose, n = 1L, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = 24 * (0:13)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = c(0, ss_grid)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

typ_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  solve_typical(arms$drug[i], ss_events(arms$dose[i])) |>
    dplyr::filter(time >= 13 * 24) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      plasma = trap(time, Cc), lesion = trap(time, Clesion), caseum = trap(time, Ccaseum)
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms$treatment[i])
}))

table_s3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~plasma_s3, ~caseum_s3, ~cellular_gransim_s3,
  "MXF 60 mg/kg",  45.1,       276.1,      609.3,
  "MXF 25 mg/kg",  18.0,       109.1,      243.7,
  "GTX 40 mg/kg",  36.0,       103.1,      192,
  "LVX 100 mg/kg", 113.3,      237.7,      325.4
)

ss_cmp <- typ_ss |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table_s3, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    plasma_pct = 100 * (plasma - plasma_s3) / plasma_s3,
    ratio_model = caseum / plasma,
    ratio_s3 = caseum_s3 / plasma_s3,
    ratio_pct = 100 * (ratio_model - ratio_s3) / ratio_s3
  )

ss_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(
    treatment, plasma, plasma_s3, plasma_pct, caseum, caseum_s3,
    ratio_model, ratio_s3, ratio_pct, lesion, cellular_gransim_s3
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-treatment, \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment,
    "Plasma AUC, model" = plasma, "Plasma AUC, Table S3" = plasma_s3,
    "Plasma diff (%)" = plasma_pct,
    "Caseum AUC, model" = caseum, "Caseum AUC, Table S3" = caseum_s3,
    "Caseum/plasma, model" = ratio_model, "Caseum/plasma, Table S3" = ratio_s3,
    "Ratio diff (%)" = ratio_pct,
    "Cellular-area AUC, model" = lesion,
    "Cellular granuloma AUC, Table S3 (GranSim)" = cellular_gransim_s3
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value steady-state AUC0-24 (mg*h/L) on day 14 against Table S3 means.")

# Deterministic typical-value solve. Realised plasma differences are -11.1% to
# +4.6% and caseum/plasma ratio differences -8.2% to -1.0%. Table S3 holds means
# over 100 sampled parameter sets, so it is not exactly a typical-value
# quantity; a transcription error in CL or in a caseum rate constant moves
# these by far more than the bounds.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss_cmp$plasma_pct) < 15),
  all(abs(ss_cmp$ratio_pct) < 10)
)
```

The cellular-granuloma AUC of Table S3 comes from GranSim, not from this
model, and the two are not expected to agree; the model's cellular-area AUC
is shown alongside for reference only.

# Replicate Figure 5A (moxifloxacin 60 versus 25 mg/kg)

```{r fig-5a}
fig5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical("moxifloxacin", ss_events(60)) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "MXF 60 mg/kg"),
  solve_typical("moxifloxacin", ss_events(25)) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "MXF 25 mg/kg")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 13 * 24) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = time - 13 * 24) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, time, Plasma = Cc, Cellular = Clesion, Caseum = Ccaseum) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, Cellular, Caseum), names_to = "site", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(fig5, aes(time, conc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~site, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the 14th daily dose (h)", y = "Moxifloxacin (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value analogue of Figure 5A of Sarathy 2019."
  )
```

The model is linear, so the 25 mg/kg profiles are the 60 mg/kg profiles scaled
by 25/60 in every compartment.

# Stochastic cohort and PKNCA against the rabbit monitoring data (Table S4)

Table S4 reports steady-state AUC0-24 and Cmax measured in the efficacy-study
rabbits (3 to 5 per arm) after 2 to 3 weeks of daily dosing. A cohort of 100
virtual rabbits per arm is simulated with between-animal variability on the
plasma parameters.

```{r stochastic}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_per_arm <- 100L

sim_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  ev <- ss_events(arms$dose[i], n = n_per_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms$treatment[i])
  rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[arms$drug[i]]](), events = ev, keep = "treatment") |>
    as.data.frame()
}))

sim_ss_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  ss_events(arms$dose[i], n = n_per_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms$treatment[i])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(sim_ss_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, Cc)

nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)

nca_dose <- sim_ss_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 13 * 24, end = 14 * 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

table_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "MXF 60 mg/kg",  43.9,     4.4,
  "MXF 25 mg/kg",  13.2,     2.6,
  "GTX 40 mg/kg",  38.5,     5.7,
  "LVX 100 mg/kg", 129,      16.8
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = table_s4,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA (day 14, 100 rabbits per arm) against the observed rabbit means of Table S4. * differs from the reference by more than 20%."
)
```

The "Simulated" column is the median over the 100 virtual rabbits of each arm.
The "Reference" column is the mean of 3 to 5 observed rabbits per arm, sampled
at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 h (Table S4 also gives the observed ranges: AUC
30.4-55.3, 8.6-17.4, 29.5-56.5 and 90-152 mg*h/L, and Cmax 3.0-6.1, 1.9-3.4,
5.0-6.4 and 10.2-21.3 mg/L, in the row order above). It is a small-sample
check, not a target. The rows that differ by more than 20% are explained as
follows:

- **Moxifloxacin 25 mg/kg AUC.** The observed mean (13.2 mg*h/L) is below the
  dose-proportional value of the observed 60 mg/kg arm (43.9 x 25/60 =
  18.3 mg*h/L). A linear model cannot reproduce that, and the paper's own
  simulation for this arm is 18.0 mg*h/L (Table S3).
- **Moxifloxacin 60 mg/kg Cmax and levofloxacin 100 mg/kg AUC.** The simulated
  medians fall inside the observed ranges of Table S4. The paper's own
  simulated levofloxacin plasma AUC (113.3 mg*h/L, Table S3) is also below the
  observed 129 mg*h/L.

No assertion is placed on this stochastic comparison. The deterministic checks
above are the validation gates.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Site-of-action ODEs.** The paper does not print the equations of the
  multi-compartment model. Figure S3A shows direct exchange between plasma and
  each site, with dashed arrows for "small physiological compartments that do
  not significantly affect plasma concentrations", and Table S1 gives a pair
  of first-order rate constants per site with no site volumes. The maintainers
  encoded each site as a concentration driven by plasma concentration,
  `d/dt(C_site) = k_central_site * Cc - k_site_central * C_site`, with no mass
  returned to plasma, following the Kjellsson 2012 lesion-penetration approach
  the paper cites. This form reproduces the single-dose curves of Figure S3B
  and the caseum-to-plasma AUC ratios of Table S3 (checks above). An
  amount-based form would need site volumes that the paper does not report.
- **Plasma model.** The two-compartment first-order-absorption ODEs are those
  of Pienaar 2017 (*Plasma PK model*). Pienaar 2017 prints the absorption term
  as `ka * Dose`; the maintainers read this as first-order absorption from a
  depot, which the text states ("two-compartment model with first-order
  absorption"). Bioavailability is not reported, so the parameters are
  apparent (oral) values and no `F` is applied.
- **Typical values and variability.** The Table S1 "mean" is taken as the
  typical (median) value of the lognormal distribution, as the Pienaar 2017
  footnote says the values were "determined by non-linear mixed effects
  modeling". The %CV is converted to a log-scale variance as
  `log(1 + CV^2)`. No correlations between random effects are reported, so
  none are included. The site-of-action rate constants have no
  between-animal variability; the paper reports 95% confidence intervals only.
- **Stochastic means.** Table S3 reports means over 100 sampled parameter
  sets that sit close to the typical-value AUC (for example 113.3 against a
  typical 100.9 mg*h/L for levofloxacin). With lognormal variability of 61%
  (gatifloxacin) and 96% (levofloxacin) on clearance, the mean of a cohort
  simulated from these models is higher than that (the mean AUC is
  `exp(omega^2 / 2)` times the typical value), so the stochastic cohort does
  not reproduce the Table S3 means for those two drugs. The paper does not
  say how its 100 parameter sets were drawn beyond "Latin hypercube sampling",
  and the maintainers did not adjust the variances to match.
- **Residual error.** The plasma fit used a constant error model whose
  magnitude is not reported; it is encoded as an additive error fixed to 0.
  The site rate constants were fitted by least squares and have no error
  model.
- **Levofloxacin lung rate constants.** Table S1 gives 95% confidence
  intervals that cross zero (k pl-lung 3.6, -6 to 13; k lung-pl 3.3, -6 to
  12), so the individual rate constants are poorly identified; their ratio
  (about 1.1) is what determines the lung exposure.
- **Units.** Doses are in mg/kg and volumes in L/kg, so concentrations are in
  mg/L, matching the paper's figures. The site states hold concentrations,
  not amounts.
- **Drug abbreviation.** The paper uses both GTX and GFX for gatifloxacin.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for Sarathy 2019 or Pienaar 2017 was found
  in Europe PMC as of 2026-11-25.
